title: CEN/CENELEC JTC 24 — EN 18216–18223, prEN 18239/18246
usedFor: Conformance target, not a term source. A harmonised-standards series is something we are tested by, not something we model in.
licence: Purchased standards. Redistribution of clause text is prohibited; the standard numbers themselves are freely citable.
source: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2026/1736 of 14 July 2026, OJ 15 July 2026, CELEX 32026D1736 (eur-lex.europa.eu) — fetched directly, cross-confirmed against CEN-CENELEC's own news page. No EN clause text read; still purchase-gated.
finding: **Corrects the prior record on two counts, both now settled against a primary source rather than a survey.** First: EN 18223 **is** cited as a harmonised standard as of 15 July 2026 — the prior 'no OJEU citation, so no presumption of conformity' claim is stale. The Decision's Annex lists six EN 182xx:2026 standards as harmonised: EN 18216 (data exchange protocols), EN 18219 (unique identifiers), EN 18220 (data carriers), EN 18221 (storage/archiving/persistence), EN 18222 (APIs), EN 18223 (system interoperability). prEN 18239 (access rights/security) and prEN 18246 (data authentication/integrity) remain draft, uncited. Second: this resolves the self-contradiction the prior record flagged about what EN 18223 covers — it is confirmed **'System Interoperability'**, meaning the voided internal document had it right and the third-party source calling it 'the DPP information model' was wrong. Legal consequence: per the Decision's own operative text, a DPP conforming to a cited standard is now presumed to conform to ESPR Arts. 10-11 to the extent that standard covers those articles — a live legal fact now, not a future contingency.
nextStep: Buy EN 18223 — unchanged as the right target (it governs passport structure and decides the UPI format question), but now higher-priority than before: a purchased read carries live legal weight today rather than optionality against an uncited standard. Currently deferred on funds, not on doubt about whether it matters — registration is separately blocked regardless (no battery semantic catalogue exists yet), so the deferral costs nothing near-term.
